title: A request that dies on a memory limit leaves the session upload-progress pointer published, and the next request URL-encodes the freed heap into a cookie
index_line: T-0076 · MEM_READ · RFC1867 upload-progress state survives an OOM abort; next request reads reclaimed worker heap into PHPSESSID · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: PHP assumed an aborted request cannot leave pre-initialisation session state behind: the upload-progress decoder publishes request-owned bookkeeping before module initialisation completes, and the fatal-error path destroys the request heap without un-defining that worker-global — so the next request on the same worker reads a pointer into freed memory.

mechanism.does: a multipart RFC1867 request carrying PHPSESSID and PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS fields reaches PHP before application code runs
the Session upload-progress handler initialises session state in the pre-initialisation window and publishes a request-owned id/string in PS(id)
a fatal out-of-memory error aborts the request before the matching cleanup runs
PHP destroys the request heap while the worker-global still points into it
a later multipart request on the same worker reaches the upload-progress cleanup path before normal Session initialisation resets the pointer
PHP treats the stale pointer and length as a live zend_string and URL-encodes the reclaimed bytes into the PHPSESSID response cookie

source.http.body.value: a multipart RFC1867 body with PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS and PHPSESSID fields, parsed before any application code

source.http.cookie.value: the PHPSESSID cookie; the same header is also the disclosure channel on the way out

sink.deser.native.value: the session upload-progress decoder that unserialises request-owned state into worker-globals

lifetime.object.value: PS(id) survives the request that owned the allocation — the use-after-free core

oracle.channel.value: the reclaimed heap is URL-encoded into a Set-Cookie PHPSESSID value the attacker can read

guard.none.value: no application code needs to run, and session_start() is not required — the bug is below the app layer

preconditions.expr: the deployment runs an affected PHP and leaves session upload-progress enabled
the PHP build is in the affected version range
the web tier accepts multipart POSTs and answers with headers

success: a Set-Cookie PHPSESSID value that decodes to bytes the attacker never sent (other clients' data, environment strings, binary)
the disclosed region is attacker-sized and repeated requests on the same worker yield different heap contents
failure_like: patched PHP returns a normal session id
upload-progress is disabled (session.upload_progress.enabled=0) so the pre-init path is never taken
false_positive: a long random-looking PHPSESSID is normal — require decoded bytes that are recognisably foreign data
a 500 from the memory limit alone is the abort, not the disclosure; the leak is observed on the following request

hazards: any worker-pool runtime that decodes request data before its per-request reset runs
the prerequisite is an abort path the attacker can trigger deterministically (memory limit, timeout, fatal error)
the output channel can be anything that echoes worker state: a header, a cookie, an error page
non_transfers: process-per-request models (CGI without a persistent worker)
runtimes that reset pre-init state unconditionally in a finally/atexit path

evidence.target: PHP core session upload-progress handling, all supported branches before the 2026-10-21 fix (CVE-2026-109618)

provenance.author: Wiz Research
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-109618 upload-progress unserializer use-after-free: Session decodes upload-progress data in the pre-initialisation window and stores request-owned bookkeeping in BG(unserialize)/PS(id); a fatal allocation failure destroys the request heap and leaves the global published; a later multipart request on the same worker URL-encodes the reclaimed heap into a PHPSESSID response cookie

provenance.author: Arctic Wolf Labs
provenance.corroborates: independent analysis of PHP2Shell: both CVEs are memory-safety bugs in PHP fatal-error handling that leave corrupted worker state for a later request; documents widescale scanning of upload-progress/session-poisoning paths and command-execution validation attempts
